explanation: The aliens speed up as fewer remain. That began as a quirk: the hardware could move a smaller group faster, and designer Tomohiro Nishikado kept it because it built tension.

claims.text: Space Invaders, released by Taito in 1978, has players shoot at rows of advancing aliens.
Asteroids, Galaga and Defender were released after 1978.
In Space Invaders the aliens move faster as fewer of them remain.
The speed-up arose because the hardware could move fewer aliens more quickly, and designer Tomohiro Nishikado kept it.

evidence.restatement: The invaders speed up as their numbers fall.
The hardware could draw fewer aliens faster, and Nishikado kept the speed-up as a feature.
Space Invaders, Tomohiro Nishikado's Taito arcade game, came out in 1978 and has the player shoot rows of descending aliens.
Asteroids dates from 1979, and Galaga and Defender from 1981.
The invaders move faster as their number falls.
Nishikado has said the speed-up was a hardware side effect (fewer sprites to redraw, so quicker movement) which he chose to keep.
